subject: EMEA: data residency + region coverage wording for benchmark report
body:
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Henry Cho <henry.cho@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jun 25, 2025 at 08:14 AM GMT+2
Subject: EMEA: data residency + region coverage wording for benchmark report

Hi Soojin,

Quick EMEA ask before we lock the landing page copy + the enablement FAQ.

1) Which EU regions are we comfortable highlighting as "available" (vs "benchmark-only" or "experimental")? I keep getting asked to be specific (Ireland vs Frankfurt) and to avoid AWS-region naming if possible.

2) Can we get approved phrasing for data residency based on deployment mode?
   - Hosted API (multi-tenant)
   - Dedicated
   - Private (VPC/on-prem)

3) APAC: should we include Singapore/Tokyo in the public tables? My EMEA pipeline (especially financial services) keeps asking "do you have APAC" and then immediately "is it GA and stable?".

I attached a 1-pager with the questions I’m hearing + the draft wording I’ve been using, but I want to align with Legal before Sales repeats something too strong.

Attachment: EMEA_region_coverage_notes_v2.docx

Thanks,
Lukas
EMEA Sales Enablement
Redwood Inference


---
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Henry Cho <henry.cho@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jun 25, 2025 at 09:02 AM GMT+2
Subject: Re: EMEA: data residency + region coverage wording for benchmark report

Thanks Lukas — super helpful.

On (1) + (3), let’s get Henry + Vanessa to confirm what we can label as "Supported" for publication vs "Included in this report".

On (2), looping in Sofia/Michael for exact residency language. Our goal is: clear + accurate, and explicit that Hosted ≠ hard residency guarantee.

I’ll consolidate + send back proposed copy for approval today.

Soojin

From: Henry Cho <henry.cho@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jun 25, 2025 at 09:38 AM GMT+2
Subject: Re: EMEA: data residency + region coverage wording for benchmark report

For the web experience + report tables, I’d suggest we separate:

A) "Regions included in benchmark" (fact for this report)
B) "Regions supported for production" (product posture)

Proposal (names in customer-friendly terms):
- EU West (Dublin)
- EU Central (Frankfurt)

These are the two I’d be comfortable calling "production supported" on Hosted/Dedicated today.

For APAC, we can show results if we have stable runs, but I would not label as "production supported" in the same way unless Vanessa confirms capacity posture. Also: we should avoid implying residency guarantees for Hosted just because a region exists.

Henry


---
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Henry Cho <henry.cho@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jun 25, 2025 at 10:21 AM GMT+2
Subject: Re: EMEA: data residency + region coverage wording for benchmark report

+1 to Henry.

Capacity/ops view (for public labeling):

OK to highlight (GA posture / we can stand behind):
- EU West (Dublin)
- EU Central (Frankfurt)

APAC:
- APAC Southeast (Singapore): we can include in the benchmark tables if the runs pass stability gates, but I recommend labeling as "Available (limited capacity)" or "Available by request" depending on what PMM/Legal are comfortable with.
- APAC Northeast (Tokyo): we’ve had intermittent supply constraints. I’d strongly prefer we do NOT put Tokyo on the public landing page as a headline region for v1. If it’s in the PDF appendix with a caveat, fine, but I don’t want AEs promising it broadly.

If we need a single line for Sales: "APAC coverage available — contact us for current region availability and capacity." (with Dedicated/Private being the right path for guarantees).

Vanessa


---
From: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Henry Cho <henry.cho@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jun 25, 2025 at 12:07 PM GMT+2
Subject: Re: EMEA: data residency + region coverage wording for benchmark report

Here’s the safe frame we should use across landing page + FAQ.

Key points:
- Avoid: "EU-only processing" / "data never leaves the EU" for Hosted, unless we have a signed DPA addendum with explicit scope (we do not for the public claim).
- Allowed: "Requests are served in the selected region" (if true), plus explicit note that operational metadata/logs may be processed/stored elsewhere depending on customer configuration and support needs.
- For Dedicated/Private, we can say "customer-selected region" and "data residency controls" but avoid "guaranteed" unless contractually committed.

Suggested wording (draft):

Hosted API:
"You can select the region where your inference requests are served (e.g., EU West/Dublin, EU Central/Frankfurt). Depending on your configuration, certain operational metadata (e.g., usage metrics, support logs) may be processed or stored in other locations. Contact Redwood for workload-specific data handling requirements."

Dedicated:
"Dedicated capacity is provisioned in a customer-selected region. Data isolation and regional deployment options are available; residency requirements can be addressed contractually."

Private (VPC/on-prem):
"Private deployments support customer-managed networking and data handling controls (VPC / on‑prem), designed for regulated or residency-constrained workloads."

We should also add a clear disclaimer on the benchmark page that region availability and performance may vary over time.

Sofia
Legal (Claims/Comparative Review)


---
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Henry Cho <henry.cho@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jun 25, 2025 at 13:44 PM GMT+2
Subject: Re: EMEA: data residency + region coverage wording for benchmark report

Agree with Sofia.

Two edits:
- Replace "may be processed or stored" with "may be processed and/or stored" (minor, but more accurate for systems that replicate).
- Add "This is not a guarantee of data residency" as a parenthetical in the Hosted section (or an FAQ entry) so it’s unambiguous.

Also: avoid implying APAC availability is continuous if we’re labeling Singapore as limited.

Michael

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Henry Cho <henry.cho@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jun 25, 2025 at 05:46 PM GMT+2
Subject: Re: EMEA: data residency + region coverage wording for benchmark report

Lukas — consolidated, approved direction below (please use this in EMEA talk tracks + we’ll port into the landing page + FAQ).

1) EU regions to highlight (public):
- Production supported: EU West (Dublin), EU Central (Frankfurt)
- On the interactive page: we’ll label these as "Supported" and note that performance numbers reflect the benchmark window.

2) Data residency phrasing (approved):

Hosted API:
"You can select the region where your inference requests are served (e.g., EU West/Dublin, EU Central/Frankfurt). Depending on your configuration, certain operational metadata (e.g., usage metrics, support logs) may be processed and/or stored in other locations. (This is not a guarantee of data residency.) Contact Redwood for workload-specific data handling requirements."

Dedicated:
"Dedicated capacity is provisioned in a customer-selected region. Data isolation and regional deployment options are available; residency requirements can be addressed contractually."

Private (VPC/on‑prem):
"Private deployments support customer-managed networking and data handling controls (VPC / on‑prem), designed for regulated or residency‑constrained workloads."

3) APAC inclusion:
- Singapore can appear in the benchmark tables if stability gates pass, but we will label it "Available (limited capacity)" and avoid headline positioning.
- Tokyo: not highlighted for v1.
- Sales line (if asked broadly): "APAC coverage is available — contact us for current region availability and capacity." (Push Dedicated/Private for guarantees.)

Action: If you’re OK, I’ll have Wei/Docs update the landing page disclaimers + add an EMEA-specific entry in the Sales FAQ by EOD tomorrow.

Soojin
Director of Product Marketing
Redwood Inference
